$comment: Each entry documents a Command that MUST be rejected, and why. 'command' (when present) is a JSON object to validate against schema/command.schema.json -- validate_fixtures.py asserts these all FAIL. 'raw' (malformed_command only) is a literal string that is not valid JSON at all, so it cannot be represented as a JSON object -- see its own note.

malformed_command.violates: must not be accepted as valid JSON at all
malformed_command.note: Deliberately truncated/malformed JSON (double comma, unterminated object). Both agents' JSON parsers (nlohmann::json) and Python's json.loads must raise a parse error, not attempt partial recovery.

missing_required_field.violates: schema/command.schema.json required list; docs/SECURITY.md invariant 14 (TERMINATE_PROCESS without start_time_ticks must translate to nothing, not a guessed KILL_PROCESS)

invalid_target_types.violates: docs/SECURITY.md invariant 4 (pid/start_time_ticks must be positive integers)
invalid_target_types.note: pid is a string, start_time_ticks is a boolean -- both must be rejected even though JSON's 'true' can coerce to 1 in some loose languages.

wrong_target_shape.violates: docs/SECURITY.md invariant 3 (target shape is determined by action)
wrong_target_shape.note: ISOLATE_HOST must carry no target at all; this smuggles a process target onto it.

smuggled_shell_field.note: additionalProperties:false at the top level must reject this outright, regardless of the shell field's content.

non_utc_timestamp.violates: docs/SECURITY.md invariant 5 (expires_at must be UTC-only; see 'Schema limitation' note -- JSON Schema alone will NOT catch this one)
non_utc_timestamp.note: This timestamp is a valid RFC 3339 date-time and passes schema/command.schema.json's format check, but both native agents reject any non-Z/+00:00 offset in their own parser code. validate_fixtures.py documents (does not silently assume) this gap.

oversized_correlation_id.violates: schema/command.schema.json's maxLength:128 on correlation_id (Phase 6 item 13, boundary fixture)
oversized_correlation_id.note: correlation_id here is 137 characters, one past the 128-character maximum.

replay_detected_scenario.violates: docs/SECURITY.md invariant 7 (a command already accepted once must be rejected on replay)
replay_detected_scenario.note: Not a single malformed payload -- this documents a two-step scenario: the SAME command_id (cmd-0001, byte-identical to fixtures/commands/valid.json's KILL_PROCESS entry) is presented to command_gate/CommandGate twice for the same agent_id. The first call must succeed (receipt_code succeeded); the second call, even though the JSON is byte-identical and independently well-formed, must be rejected with replay_detected. A durable ledger must preserve this across a process restart between the two calls (see panopticon-linux-agent's replay_ledger and panopticon-agent's ReplayLedger).

cross_agent_mismatch.violates: docs/SECURITY.md invariant 8 (a command addressed to a different agent_id/host_id must be rejected)
cross_agent_mismatch.note: This command's agent_id is 'agent-linux-01'. A command_gate constructed for a DIFFERENT agent (e.g. 'agent-windows-01') must reject it, even though the JSON itself is well-formed and would be valid if received by the correct agent.

correlation_mismatch.violates: docs/SECURITY.md invariant 9 (a result's correlation_id must match the stored command's correlation_id)
correlation_mismatch.note: Scenario, not a single payload: the command fixtures/commands/valid.json's COLLECT_PROCESS_INFO entry (correlation_id 'corr-0002') is dispatched, but the agent submits a CommandResult with correlation_id 'corr-9999' -- a confused-deputy attempt to attach a result to a command it doesn't actually belong to (or a genuine bug). Manager's /command-results handler must reject this result outright.
correlation_mismatch.expected_outcome: rejected by Manager (result never applied to the command's lifecycle_state)
